contentBlocks.text: You've identified purpose and audience. Today: specific techniques media uses to persuade!

Persuasive media often uses recognizable techniques: emotional appeal (targeting a feeling, like yesterday's 'tired and stuck'), loaded language (words with strong positive or negative connotations, like 'champions'), and selective framing (choosing which facts to include or leave out to support a particular impression). Read this new example: 'Don't miss out — join thousands of satisfied customers before this limited-time offer disappears forever!' Identify at least two different persuasive techniques used in this sentence, and name which one each is.
You just identified real persuasive techniques in media! Tomorrow we'll analyze a complete example using everything from this week.

objectives: Name three persuasive techniques: emotional appeal, loaded language, selective framing
Identify at least two techniques within the 'limited-time offer' example sentence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's how/purpose/audience work briefly.
2. Introduce the three persuasive techniques with clear definitions.
3. Have the child identify at least two techniques in the example sentence.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's combined-analysis lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: point to 'don't miss out' and 'disappears forever' specifically and ask what feeling (urgency, fear of missing out) they create, before asking for independent identification
Ready for more: ask the child to rewrite the sentence removing all three techniques, keeping only the neutral factual content
This connects directly back to Grade 9's rhetoric/ethos-pathos-logos content, applying similar analysis skills to a media context specifically
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended analysis activity — check that the child identifies at least two genuine techniques, such as emotional appeal ('don't miss out' creating urgency/fear of missing out), loaded language ('satisfied customers,' 'limited-time'), or selective framing (only mentioning satisfaction, never any downside).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 9-10 RI.9-10.8: delineating and evaluating the reasoning and specific claims in a persuasive text, continuing this week's media-analysis thread.
